text:
Chicago had gone six games without a win (0-5-1) before Thursday, and Ryan Donato ended the run 3:12 into overtime at the United Center, finishing a wrist shot off a feed from Anton Frondell and Sam Rinzel for a 3-2 win over Buffalo. Donato, a second-round pick of Boston in 2014 who scored 21 goals in 36 games at Harvard, played just 11:18 but made the one shot that counted.

Frank Nazar did the rest of the damage, scoring both regulation goals: a power-play wrist shot in the first period and a third-period tip-in that tied it at 2-2. The Blackhawks trailed after one period, and the early play favored Buffalo. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the count of shots, were 0.78 to 0.39 for the Sabres in the first and 0.73 to 0.38 in the second. Buffalo finished with 51 shot attempts to Chicago's 40. But Chicago owned the third, out-chancing the Sabres 1.18 to 0.59, and added 0.52 more in overtime. Over the full game our numbers say Chicago deserved to win 57 percent of the time, meaning it took the larger share of simulated replays of every shot. Spencer Knight stopped 21 of 23 and finished a shade ahead of what the chances should have produced.

For Chicago, the winless run is over, and it came against a Buffalo team that beat it 4-3 in the October meeting. The Blackhawks looked like the stronger side once the game opened up late. The Sabres outshot their way to a lead, got power-play goals from Tage Thompson and a slap shot from Owen Power, and lost anyway. We'd watch whether they can turn all that territorial play into goals.
